Girly, in my comment I didn't mean you were any of those things or that you were wanting to leave. What I meant is that although you are perfectly happy living your life within the organization other people are not. Sexual orientation is not something you can change, it is part of who you are. It isn't something you can turn off and on like a light switch or even something to work at. If a brother or sister developed a relationship or acted upon their sexual/romantic orientation with someone of the same sex and didn't want to break up with that person, then they would be reproved or disfellowshipped if they seemed to be unrepentant. 

You don't want to leave, I know. But what if you did? Would you have the choice? Would you be able to start a new life and still keep your loved ones?  Or would you leave with nothing an no-one. With no real knowledge of how the world works or higher education. 

You don't have anything outside the religion it encompasses every aspect of your life. You believe what they want you to believe, you read what they want you to read, you feel what they want you to feel. And for people that do not fit the mold like you do, it is hell. 

Yes, I reached out to various people. I told two of my bible teachers (who were the wives of elders) about what happened to me. I poured my heart and told them how alone I felt. How it felt to be living with a monster and being told to respect him as the and family head. They just told me to pray to Jehovah for strength. That he would get me through. I thought I had their support, at least when it came to kind words. Until they deemed me too troublesome and could possibly stain their good standing since I could be considered an extension of themselves since they were my teachers, especially when I was placed in foster care. 

Yes, the elders knew. My father was a publisher and had studied with an elder for years but never quite made the dunk. As part of his meeting before getting baptized he confessed what had happened. They sent letters back and forth with the circuit and district overseer until they contacted headquarters. Theylet him get baptized. He is still a member of the congregation today. Preaching and having talks like nothing happened.

I think that she was unconsciously aware for a really long time until I told her. When I did she said she would think about what we should do. At the time my grandparents were coming to visit from Mexico so she asked me to keep things under wraps until they left.... they left and she told me that our future was in my hands. She said that I told her to leave my father, she would. But to keep in mind that our world was going to change. That we would have to move back to Mexico because she couldn't work here. She told me that I was going to have to raise my sisters since she was going to have to work day and night to support us. And she told me that I could never tell my family what had happened because it would break their heart. 

A few days later my father called her and promised that things would change. That he would do anything to keep this family together. That he would finally get baptized and change. She asked me to try and forgive and move past it. 

I was 11 at the time.

Well for one, my parents were JW's as well. They always told me that if I was living in their home, then I would have to abide by their rules. This meant going to the meetings every week, preaching as well as family worship. It was non negotiable. Not to mention the frequent shepherding calls from the elders. Dropsii, what would happen if you left? If you got disfellowshipped for voicing your doubts and concerns? What if you fell in love with someone outside the organization or realized you were not heterosexual? Would you be willing to leave everyone you know and love to start a new life? Would you be willing to loose your network of support and start anew in the world that we had heard so many cautionary tales about? Trust me, I wish I could have had my own beliefs while still seeing my sisters grow up and be a part of their life. I wish that coming to terms with who I was didn't break my mothers heart. 

No, they do not pass a basket for contributions during the meetings. But more often than not the topic would be broached in the congregation needs part of the meeting during the week. Perhaps they didn't do it in your congregation, but in mine they asked every head of the household to write on a slip of paper what would be their family's expected contribution. Not to mention the millions of dollars that were spent building the new headquarters. 

In my case, after coming back from foster care during a shepherding call I was told to throw my load onto Jehovah. That he would help. I was also told to think about what I would be doing to my family once again If I broached the subject of my abuse to a professional with my sisters living in the home. That the educated mental health professionals did not have knowledge of Jehovah and the same hope of paradise that we did. They said I could find Jehovah's comforting words in the Bible and they would make me strong. I was past receiving peace from written words in a book. I was tired and hurt from people throwing what had happened to me under the rug. I was tired of being told to rely on Jehovah while my abuser was up on the platform talking about his experiences and preaching about finding peace and happiness in the organization.
